seoDescription: Learn how to create a fully customized camera preview overlay in your Ionic and Capacitor applications. This tutorial guides you through using the Capacitor Community Camera Preview plugin to add custom elements like logos, buttons, and other UI controls directly on top of the live camera feed. You'll see how to handle potential issues with the plugin, configure it for both Android and iOS, and use specific CSS techniques, including z-index and `::part`, for styling web components to position your overlay correctly.

chapters.title: Introduction to Custom Camera Overlays
chapters.description: Learn why a custom plugin is needed for camera overlays and get an overview of the Capacitor Community Camera Preview plugin and its initial setup.

chapters.title: Setting Up and Opening the Camera Preview
chapters.description: This chapter covers importing the necessary modules, defining states, and implementing the `openCamera` function with its required HTML container.

chapters.title: Adding UI Elements to the Overlay
chapters.description: Implement the HTML for a custom user interface, including a logo and buttons for capturing, flipping, and stopping the camera.

chapters.title: Styling the Overlay with CSS and ::part
chapters.description: Apply CSS to correctly position overlay elements using absolute positioning and z-index, and learn to style inside web components with `::part`.

chapters.title: Implementing Camera Control Functions
chapters.description: Write the functions for capturing an image, stopping the camera, and flipping between front and rear cameras, and debug a z-index issue.

chapters.title: Final Demo on a Physical Device
chapters.description: See the application running on a real mobile device, demonstrating the custom overlay with its capture, flip, and stop functionality.

chapters.title: Outro & Ionic Academy
chapters.description: Concluding remarks and a call to action to like, subscribe, and check out the Ionic Academy for more in-depth courses.

summary:
## The Goal: A Custom Camera UI The standard Capacitor camera plugin opens the native device camera UI, which doesn't allow for custom branding or controls. This guide uses the **Capacitor Community Camera Preview plugin** to render the camera feed directly within the app's web view, enabling the creation of a fully custom HTML and CSS overlay. ## Core Technology: Capacitor Camera Preview - **Plugin**: `@capacitor-community/camera-preview` - **Function**: Starts the camera in the background of the web view, allowing your HTML content to act as an overlay. > [!NOTE] The plugin may have unresolved issues or missing features in its web implementation compared to native. For example, the `flip()` function works on iOS/Android but may not be defined in the web interface. ## Setup & Configuration 1. **Install Plugin**: `npm install @capacitor-community/camera-preview` 2. **Add Platforms**: Run `ionic build` and `npx cap add ios android`. 3. **Configure Android**: You must register the plugin in your `android/app/.../MainActivity.java` file by adding the provided initialization code block. ## Implementation Steps ### HTML Structure The plugin needs a specific DOM element to attach the camera preview to. > [!IMPORTANT] You must include an empty `
` in your page's HTML. The plugin searches for this specific ID to render the camera feed. ### TypeScript Logic - **Import**: Import `Plugins`, `CameraPreview`, and `CameraPreviewOptions` from the appropriate packages. - **Start Camera**: Call `CameraPreview.start(options)` with options like: - `parent`: 'camera-preview' (The ID of the div). - `position`: 'rear' or 'front'. - **Capture Image**: Call `CameraPreview.capture({ quality: 90 })`. The result is a Base64 string. - **Display Image**: To display the captured image in an `` tag, you must prepend the Base64 data with `data:image/jpeg;base64,`. - **Stop Camera**: Call `CameraPreview.stop()` to close the preview and release the camera. ### Styling the Overlay with CSS - **Transparent Background**: To see the camera preview behind your web content, make the web view background transparent. For Ionic, this can be done by targeting `ion-content`: ```css ion-content { --background: transparent; } ``` - **Positioning Elements**: Use `position: absolute` on all overlay elements (buttons, images, etc.) to place them at specific coordinates over the camera view. > [!TIP] > Use `z-index` to control the stacking order. The camera view can sometimes cover your HTML elements. Give your interactive overlay buttons a higher `z-index` (e.g., `z-index: 11`) than other elements to ensure they are on top and clickable. - **Styling Shadow DOM with `::part`**: To style elements inside a Web Component's Shadow DOM (like Ionic components), you can use the `::part()` pseudo-element. This allows you to apply styles to a component's internal, named parts. - **Example**: Make an `ion-button` round. ```css ion-button::part(native) { border-radius: 50%; } ```
